backward_compat_traps.rule: Public LoRaWAN uses sync word 0x34; private networks use 0x12.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A device with the wrong sync word will not detect frames from the intended network.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Every end-device must implement Class A; B and C are supersets.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming a Class C device can drop Class A behavior breaks interoperability.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Regional duty-cycle limits (e.g. 1% EU868) bound airtime.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Ignoring the duty cycle is non-compliant and degrades the shared network.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The frame counter must strictly increase; the receiver rejects non-increasing counters as replays.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Resetting FCnt without a rejoin (ABP) causes the server to reject frames.

backward_compat_traps.rule: OTAA derives fresh session keys at join; ABP uses static keys.
backward_compat_traps.trap: ABP's static keys are weaker; treating ABP as equivalent to OTAA security is wrong.

fields.spec_version: LoRa PHY (Semtech CSS) + LoRaWAN L2 1.0.4 (LoRa Alliance, 2020) + Regional Parameters
previous_versions: LoRaWAN 1.0 (2015) — initial MAC (OTAA/ABP, Classes A/B/C, ADR, AES-128).

key_changes.summary: Errata and security/identifier clarifications (JoinEUI naming formerly AppEUI, key derivation); same CSS PHY, Classes A/B/C, OTAA/ABP, ADR, and AES-128 security.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Adds rejoin, separate network/application session keys (FNwkSIntKey / SNwkSIntKey / NwkSEncKey), and roaming; backward-compatible PHY.

fields.version_naming_history_note: The LoRa PHY (Chirp Spread Spectrum) is a stable Semtech proprietary layer; the LoRaWAN MAC is an open LoRa Alliance standard layered on top. LoRaWAN 1.0 (2015) established OTAA/ABP, Classes A/B/C, ADR, and AES-128 security; 1.0.4 (2020) added errata and identifier/security clarifications; the parallel 1.1 (2017) branch added rejoin, split session keys, and roaming.
